capabilities: Navigate folders and files via title-bar or status-bar breadcrumb menus
Open, rename, move, and drag files and folders with keyboard or mouse
Preview notes in sequence with quick-preview mode using PageUp/PageDown
Browse the vault root or current folder through six hotkeyable commands
Show and select folder notes when navigating into folders
disambiguation: Not a search-and-open tool like the Quick Switcher; it browses folder contents through title-bar breadcrumb menus.
extras: Detailed compatibility notes: some themes hide or recolor the title bar making the UI unreadable, and menu colors may be too bright in some themes; CSS snippet workarounds may be needed. Mouse Ctrl/Cmd+hover preview requires the built-in Page Preview plugin.
intentEvidence: you can then do almost anything that can be done with Obsidian's built-in file explorer
motivation: The author found the built-in file explorer mouse-only and cumbersome when working with the current folder or its parents, especially with many folders and files.
problem: Obsidian's built-in file explorer is almost entirely mouse-driven, awkward for keyboard use, and slow to browse folders with many files.

relations.evidence: other Obsidian plugins such as Note Folder Autorename can be used to help create or maintain them
you can turn them off using the Style Settings plugin
if you're using a plugin like Custom Window Title that manipulates the window title directly

summary: Title-bar file explorer that shows breadcrumb paths, opens menus for files and folders, and supports keyboard navigation and quick previewing.
